title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: PLAC — omitted paradise words; condition ≠ promised justice
pass_a_gloss: And so he had inserted these words, constituted in the state of integral nature, and had subjoined those things also to be enjoyed in the earthly paradise, which why they were omitted by the learned man, I leave to others to judge. They certainly hint that the conservation of the moral integrity of Nature is presupposed, that the continuation of all the remaining goods to be enjoyed in the earthly paradise is promised. For, that I may prove the denied Minor, if God was threatening Adam as a penalty with the loss or privation of original justice, certainly he was promising as a reward the non-loss or conservation of original justice; how then could it happen that Adam should lose it? He was promising, you will say, under a condition. Which? if he persevered in integrity and justice? If he remained in obedience toward God? If he did not sin? By whatever name you call it, it will be the same as the thing promised, and the condition of the promise will be confused with the thing promised.
pass_b_english: So Amyraut had inserted the words "constituted in the state of integral nature," and had added "and those things to be enjoyed in the earthly paradise"—why the learned man omitted them I leave others to judge. They clearly presuppose conservation of nature's moral integrity and promise continuance of the remaining goods to be enjoyed in the earthly paradise.

To prove the denied minor: if God threatened Adam, as penalty, with loss or privation of original justice, then as reward He was promising non-loss—conservation—of that justice. How then could Adam lose it? "He promised under a condition," you say. Which? If he persevered in integrity and justice? Remained obedient to God? Did not sin? Call it what you will: it is the same as the thing promised, and the condition of the promise is confused with the thing promised.
source_text: Itaque inseruerat haec verba, in statu integrae naturae constituti, & subiunxerat ista eaque in paradiso Terrestri fruenda, quae cur sint a Viro Docto omissa, aliis judicandum relinquo. Innuunt certe supponi integritatis moralis Naturae conservationem, promitti reliquorum omnium bonorum in paradiso Terrestri fruendorum continuationem. Nam, ut Minorem negatam probem, si comminabatur Deus Adamo tanquam poenam, amissionem seu privationem justitiae originalis, certe pollicebatur tanquam praemium, non-amissionem seu conservationem justitiae originalis, quomodo igitur fieri potuit ut eam Adamus amitteret? Pollicebatur, inquies, sub conditione. Quanam? si perseveraret in integritate & justitia? Si permaneret in obedientia erga Deum? Si non peccaret? Quocunque nomine eam voces, idem erit cum re promissa, & conditio promissionis cum re promissa confundetur.
